pages.label: 01 / Purpose
pages.title: Make the archive usable. Keep the evidence intact.
pages.intro: The initial collection retains 105 published Stapfer transcriptions. A second workbook now supplies 2,245 transcription groups with 14,743 answer rows.
bullets: The source record remains inspectable beside the answer.
A question produces a trace, citations and a reviewable result.
All 19 local collection checks passed. The 58 missing-answer rows remain recorded; they are not negative historical evidence.
pages.caption: Actual redesigned workspace, 19 October 2026. This capture used 8B before 70B was selected as default.

pages.label: 02 / Provenance
pages.title: Every transformation needs a trail.
pages.intro: A local 202-page PDF test passed 34 ingestion, review and export checks without provider transfer. Synthetic-page OCR passed 24 checks; text boxes and table candidates remain reviewable derivatives.
bullets: Keep the original text alongside a separately normalized representation.
Use actual page locators for paginated uploads; this transcription sample has page:null.
Export citations, passage offsets, review decisions and evidence-status fields together.
pages.caption: Actual archive UI with a generated three-page fixture. Original page, extracted text and review stay separate; the fixture contains no historical facts.

pages.label: 03 / Method
pages.title: A workflow that can be inspected and corrected.
pages.intro: Apertus 70B is the default researcher. Planning, source reading, verification and optional proposals are bounded and recorded. Astra is an explicit backup or comparison choice.
bullets: Validate source identifiers, exact quotations and hashes mechanically.
Treat source text and tool output as untrusted data.
Keep doubtful interpretations under review; do not convert suggestions into source facts.
pages.caption: Actual active research before completion. Status and trace visibility are observable; correctness still requires source checks.

pages.label: 04 / Results
pages.title: Show successful checks and clear failures.
pages.intro: Tool-capable Apertus 70B passed 13/14 source-passage or expected-abstention checks;8B passed 6/14. Astra passed 14/14 as an explicit comparator.
bullets: Apertus 70B is the default, selected on this small reference. The same source was used for selection and evaluation; stronger independent testing is still needed.
Earlier public runs retained one JSON-contract failure and one completed answer rejected for unsupported interpretation. Export acceptance and rejection guards were exercised.
The earlier 35-case comparison has 19 completions and 16 failures. It is a smoke test, not a held-out benchmark.
pages.caption: Dated measurements from retained receipts. Different source/runtime snapshots are not ranked as a single quality benchmark.

pages.label: 05 / System
pages.title: Keep capabilities behind clear boundaries.
pages.intro: The public web routes to private backend, database, core and covenant services. Core owns provider access; OpenClaw requests model work through core.
bullets: HTTPS, private gRPC and WebSocket events connect the application.
Only web is public; completed runs persist in PostgreSQL and core journals use a mounted share.

Synthetic-audio WebRTC was exercised publicly. A separate local Nemotron 3 CPU test identified two anonymous speakers over four synthetic turns. No physical microphone fidelity or real-world diarization accuracy was measured.
pages.caption: Actual public synthetic-audio browser test. This does not establish physical microphone or diarization performance.

pages.label: 06 / Next evidence
pages.title: Earn stronger claims with stronger tests.
pages.intro: The next evaluation needs a frozen, licensed page corpus, independent expert labels and declared machine specifications.
bullets: Measure page structure, handwriting flags, missing-page detection and metadata accuracy.
Keep train, development and held-out evaluation partitions separate.
Publish failures, compute limits and review outcomes with every dataset release.
pages.caption: References describe external methods and models. Their published performance is not an Oldif result.
